geographies: India (all wheat-growing regions); India: Lower Gangetic Plain, West Bengal (one site); global (field-experiment sites; global extrapolation); global (spring wheat only); global gridded; regional patterns (South Asia, North China Plain, northern USA/Canada); global; country estimates for India, Russia, USA, France, China
coverage_note: Six rows from six studies: three global multi-model or multi-method studies (Zhao 2017, Jagermeyr 2021, Deryng 2014), one global sensitivity study (Asseng 2015, abstract), and two India studies (Naresh Kumar 2014 nationwide, abstract; Chandran 2023 one site, full). Without CO2 the evidence agrees on losses, with India among the more sensitive countries. With CO2 (Jagermeyr, Deryng), global and high-latitude wheat gains.
gaps: No verified wheat-specific future study for Russia, Egypt or Brazil beyond the global studies; no study at 2041-2060 SSP2-4.5 with a single CMIP6 GCM; no India study with CMIP6.

geographies: India (irrigated and rainfed rice regions); India: Lower Gangetic Plain, West Bengal (one site); global gridded; regional patterns; global; countries incl. India, China, Bangladesh
coverage_note: Four rows: Zhao 2017 (India large per-C loss; China/Bangladesh small), Jagermeyr 2021 (global ~0, gains in South Asia with CO2), Soora 2013 (India irrigated -7 % by 2050, rainfed marginal; abstract), Chandran 2023 (one West Bengal site; spans zero without CO2, gains with CO2). gaps: No verified future study for Nigeria, Italy, USA or Brazil rice specifically; no Bangladesh-specific projection read; no CMIP6 India rice study verified.

geographies: Brazil (by biome/region); global gridded; regional patterns; global suitability; USA/North America, China, Brazil, India; global; USA, China, Brazil, India; global; top producers (USA, China, Brazil); global; top producers/exporters USA, China, Brazil, Argentina, Ukraine; India in Table 1
coverage_note: Six rows: Zhao 2017, Jagermeyr 2021, Deryng 2014 (shared thresholds), Tigchelaar 2018 (closest method; USA/China/Brazil/Ukraine/India), Ramirez-Cabral 2017 (suitability), Zilli 2020 (Brazil production). The literature agrees on losses in the USA and Brazil and on maize being the most heat-sensitive cereal. gaps: No verified South Africa-specific future maize study (only Africa-wide statements); no Ukraine study beyond Tigchelaar's export analysis; no India-specific process-model study verified.
